name: Qatari Nationality by Naturalisation (Law No. 38 of 2005, Article 2)

requirements.blocker_text: 25 consecutive years of continuous legal residence (absences of up to 2 months/year permitted without breaking the clock; an absence of more than 6 months after filing risks forfeiting accrued residence).
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 25 years of continuous legal residence.

requirements.blocker_text: Good reputation; no honor-related criminal convictions.

evidence_required.document: Proof of 25 years' continuous legal residence

sources.title: American University in Cairo, Center for Migration and Refugee Studies -- verbatim English translation of Law No. 38 of 2005 on the Acquisition of Qatari Nationality: Article 2 (25yr residence, lawful income, good reputation, Arabic proficiency), Article 17 (annual cap of 50 naturalisations/year), Article 6 (discretionary grounds, dual-citizenship exception), Article 11-12 (loss of nationality)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Qatar). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to an academic center's verbatim translation of the primary law text (AUC CMRS) cross-checked against a second academic/research consortium (GLMM), both treated as tier-2 (reproduction of primary legal text by a research institution, not the institution's own legal authority -- consistent with this dataset's established convention for academic/NGO hosts of verbatim government legal text). Al Meezan, Qatar's own official legal portal (tier-1, almeezan.qa) hosts this law but was unreachable in this build (robots.txt/SSL error) -- re-attempting that fetch is the top priority for upgrading this file to published. DISTINCTIVE, PROMINENTLY FLAGGED FINDING: Article 17 caps ordinary naturalisation at A MAXIMUM OF 50 PEOPLE PER CALENDAR YEAR -- likely the single most restrictive naturalisation cap found anywhere in this dataset to date, well below Qatar's own 100/year permanent-residence cap (see qa_permanent_residence.json). No formally published application PROCESS exists for this route per multiple secondary sources -- itself a notable transparency gap in how the law operates in practice, not just a sourcing limitation on this dataset's part. dual_citizenship_allowed is FALSE for this standard route (Qatar's general rule); the discretionary Article 6 grounds are a stated EXCEPTION -- see qa_citizenship_special_grounds.json.
